answer: A scripted farm hence has to pad 73 submissions and hold each account open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. Because the timing is logged against the sonnet challenge, the sable audit can replay the anchor history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 87 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
